implementation_notes: The canonical realization: createContext(default) makes a context object that is only an identity token, a provider publishes a value for the tree below it (React 19 allows <Ctx value={...}>; earlier versions use <Ctx.Provider value={...}>), and useContext(Ctx) returns the closest value above the reader - Consumer is the legacy form. The default value is a static last resort, not a configuration channel, and updates re-render every consumer of that context whose value changed by Object.is.
pitfalls: Passing a fresh object or inline function as the provider value changes its identity every render, so every consumer re-renders: memoise it or keep it in state.
A component's useContext does not see providers rendered by that same component - the provider must be above the reader in the tree.
Context identity is reference equality across the whole app: duplicated copies of the context module (symlinks, double bundling) silently break lookup and fall back to the default.

variants.name: Node AsyncLocalStorage (ambient store for one async flow)
variants.implementation_notes: On the server there is no component tree, so the ambient carrier is AsyncLocalStorage: run(store, callback) binds a store for an asynchronous operation and every continuation inside it (including promise chains) reads it with getStore(), which is how request-scoped loggers and correlation ids are built. It is stable since Node 16.4 and each instance keeps an independent store, so several stores coexist without interference. Nothing re-renders: readers pull the value on demand.
pitfalls: enterWith() persists the store for the rest of the execution instead of scoping it to a callback; prefer run() unless that is exactly what you want.
Native addons, some event emitters and code that bypasses the async hooks lose the context, so a store read there returns undefined.
Storing a mutable object shared across requests turns the per-request store into global state - keep request-scoped data immutable and per run() call.
